# Terminal-first delivery

*Host-bound execution: treat the judged environment as the source of truth; move bytes
safely; recover fast when the shell lies or quotes bite.*

For benchmarks where correctness is **what landed on disk** and **what the test runner
said**, not what the model remembers.

## Reach the right machine

- Know whether the task runs **in-container** or **via remote shell**. Match your commands
  to that contract every time.
- One upfront map: roots, source, tests, scripts, config. No deep guesses before the map.
- If reads come back empty, first hypothesis is **wrong layer** (cwd, host, wrapper), not
  “missing file.”

## Safe writes

- Prefer compose → transfer → **read-back** for non-trivial content. Shell quoting destroys
  triple quotes, backticks, and `$`.
- Tiny edits: in-place tools the environment supports (`sed -i`, editor) rather than
  re-pasting megabytes through the terminal.
- After any write, confirm with `cat`, checksum, or the compiler/test that consumes the file.

## Parallel reads, serial writes

Independent reads in one batch. One write lane per file or coherent change set: patch,
verify, then next patch.

## Incident rule

Two identical failures on the same command shape → **stop repeating**; switch tactic
( different path, different tool, smaller repro). The third attempt must not be a copy of
the first two.

## Scope

Touch only what the ticket authorises. Production bar on changed lines. No unrelated
test churn or cosmetic sweeps.

## Proof

Run the task’s test or build. If none exists, use the tightest honest substitute (lint,
typecheck, minimal repro binary). Read failure text to the end before editing again.

## Git

Explicit staging paths; identity configured; messages one line unless specified.

## Handoff

Leave at most one short durable note when you learned a non-obvious invariant; otherwise
silence is fine.

## Stop

Green checks on the requested surface, bytes verified — exit.
